phase: Phase 1: Allow list in the guard
summary: Phase 1 passes Review B (security). The whole-segment path match, the `..` resolution, the five entry rules, and the fail-open read of measure/guard-allow resist every probe I ran or read. A path outside the listed folders can never pass; a broken or hostile list file only denies more. Three Minor items remain, all about entries an operator may legally write, plus the inherited relative-path-base limit of Review A, whose security effect I judged deny-more-only with a probe.

evidence: audited_head_sha 241282e57a56d3ec0647102179af3469b9a65608 equals git rev-parse HEAD on feat/guard-allow-list; the audited HEAD is current. Commits after role_base 470d4a4 are 88435b0, c59ee94 (tests only), and 241282e (plan.md and metadata.json only), so no production file changed after the implementation at b44ac93 and docs at ceccfdc.

Path matching: isAllowed (mods/measure-guard/hooks/guards.ts:31) resolves both sides with joinPath and matches with isInside (`p === f || p.startsWith(f + '/')`), so the match is whole-segment and case-sensitive. No startsWith shortcut exists; the adversarial record shows mutation X1 (startsWith) is caught by B2, B5, V1, V4.

Prefix and sibling tricks: B2, B5, and the adversarial path probes cover work.md, work-old/, workx/, Work/, a sibling root <root>2, /repo2, and /repos; all deny. I re-read the code; isInside needs a full `/` after the folder, so a sibling or prefix name cannot pass.

.. segments: rule 2 of allowProblem (parse.ts:41) ignores every entry with a `..` segment. joinPath (parse.ts:23) pops `..` and stops at the start, so a written path that climbs above the root resolves outside the root and isInside returns false. My probe confirmed: relative and absolute climb paths (`scripts/daily-report/work/../../../../etc/passwd`) give isAllowed false. The adversarial record shows the same for an absolute escape to /etc/passwd.

Fail-open read: readAllow (register.tsx:69 and snapshot.ts:62) wraps exists and read in try/catch and returns the empty list on any error, so a broken list can only deny more, never allow. My loader-level probe over a real temporary git repository: a missing file, a folder at the guard-allow path, and a chmod-000 file each give the empty list with no throw and parseError null. The adversarial record covers read-error and the loader tests F1, M3, M4 cover the return sites.

Binary and large list files: my probe fed binary bytes and a 50 000-line file to loadSnapshot. The loader never threw and parseError stayed null. The binary file produced one spurious folder entry (`%`) from the bytes `%\n`; a 50 000-line list parsed in 29 317 ms on this loaded machine (7 981 ms in the adversarial run). Both are availability-only effects on an operator-owned file; see finding F3.

Accepted residual risk (Decisions 6 and 15): measure/guard-allow sits inside measure/, so editDecision exempts a write to it and no check detects a list edit by the agent. I confirmed no deny text names the list: guards.ts has no `guard-allow` string (grep exit 1), and tests B2 and B3 compare each deny with a control and assert not.toContain('guard-allow'). The adversarial record shows a write to measure/guard-allow without a `[~]` task is allowed (P11), as the spec accepts.

README claims: both README sections state the limit, not a protection: 'No deny text names the list' and 'The check does not find a change of measure/guard-allow made by an agent'. Neither README says the guard protects the list. Both state the symbolic link limit: 'The guard does not resolve symbolic links' and 'No symbolic link resolution'. The adversarial record confirms a symlink inside an allowed folder to src/ is allowed (P10), matching the documented limit.

A2 (consent-blind publish gate): not applicable. No draft-to-published status flip and no consent artifact exist in this track; the test strategy records A2 as not applicable, and the diff has no publish gate.

A6 (registry overstatement): measure/tracks.md holds only the track entry and its link for this track; it claims no security state is resolved. The plugin README line 98 has the broken code span that Review A already recorded (cosmetic only).

Inherited item R-A-1 (relative path base), security judgment: isAllowed joins a relative path with snapshot.root, while commitDecision and turnProblems receive git-root-relative paths. My probe with a session root deeper than the git root shows the real allowed path is denied (deny more). The theoretical opposite case, a git-root-relative `../scripts/...` string, resolves above the wrong base to a path outside the listed folder and is also denied, so the misalignment cannot let a path outside the listed folder pass. Git cannot stage a `../` path, so no realistic allow case exists. The effect is fail-closed only; it stays nonblocking.
A3: I parsed no count by a bare digit; all counts come from labeled bun test output. A7: no shipped code path filters by a banned word.

Suites at audited HEAD: the two allow test files give 46 pass, 0 fail. The adversarial record gives the full gates at c59ee94: 131 pass plugin, 91 pass mod, tsc exit 0, parity ok, spec review gate 10 suites. HEAD adds measure/ files only.

nonblocking_findings: F1 [Nit] review-a R-A-1, judged for security (mods/measure-guard/hooks/guards.ts:31, :234, :373): isAllowed joins a relative path with snapshot.root, but commitDecision and turnProblems get git-root-relative paths. Security effect: deny too much only. My probe shows a genuinely allowed path denied under a deeper session root, and the only theoretical allow case (a `../` git-root-relative string) resolves to a path outside the listed folder and is denied. No path outside the listed folder can pass, so this stays a correctness limit, not an allow escape. Inherited from Review A; no regression in this diff.

F2 [Nit] wide legal entries (parse.ts allowProblem keeps them by design): an operator entry `.git/` would let an agent write into .git (for example .git/hooks/pre-commit) without a `[~]` task, because the edit guard then exempts the path; git executes hooks, so this is a real privilege step, though it needs the operator to write the entry first. `node_modules/` writes are invisible to the end-of-turn check (git ignores them), and a `measure/` entry is redundant because measure/ is already exempt. The spec keeps them legal (the operator owns the list); report them to the user as Minor items, not blocks.

F3 [Nit] loader content robustness (register.tsx:69, snapshot.ts:62): readAllow accepts any bytes. A line of a binary or hostile list file that ends with `/` becomes a folder entry (my probe made the entry `%` from binary bytes), and a 50 000-line list costs seconds per guarded call (adversarial finding F2: O(n*n) dedupe). Both effects deny more or slow the session only; the operator owns the file. Availability only.
